meta.tagline: Learn how to speak like a local.

categories.title: Ordering a beer/food like a local
categories.description: Q → A → what they'll probably say

situation.en: You're at a bar and the bartender asks what you're drinking.

answers.en: A small draft beer, please — how locals order.

situation.en: You've ordered a beer and they ask whether you want it draft or bottled.
The bartender asks whether you want a lager or an amber.
The bartender asks if you want anything else.

answers.es: Sí: una tapa de tortilla, porfa.

situation.en: They ask whether you're staying or taking it away.
Your glass is empty and the bartender offers another.
It's time to pay and they ask how you're paying.

question.en: How do you want to pay?

situation.en: The waiter comes over and offers you the check.

question.en: The check? / Do you want the check?

items.en: Thanks, boss. (very casual — use with care)
What a regular actually says — "put me a caña".
What do you recommend? — the fastest route to eating well.

items.es: Una clara, que aprieta el calor.
items.en: A shandy — it's baking out there.

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: You're at a café counter and the barista asks what you want.

answers.en: An espresso with a splash of milk.

exchanges.notes: "Solo" = straight espresso; "cortado" = with a little milk; "con leche" = latte-ish.

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: You've ordered a coffee and they ask how you want it.

exchanges.notes: "Café con hielo" = they give you a hot espresso and a glass of ice to pour it over.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: It's morning at a café and you want to know what they do for breakfast.

question.en: Do you have anything for breakfast?

likelyReply.es: Tostada con tomate o con mantequilla.
likelyReply.en: Toast with tomato or with butter.

exchanges.notes: "Tostada con tomate" is the classic Spanish breakfast.

situation.en: You've asked for a coffee and they want to know how you take it.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: It's late afternoon and you don't want to be awake at three.

answers.en: From the machine or a sachet?

exchanges.notes: Spain genuinely asks this. "De máquina" is the one you want — de sobre is instant stirred into hot milk.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: It's forty degrees and a hot coffee is unthinkable.

question.en: Could I get a coffee with ice?

exchanges.notes: It arrives as a hot espresso and a separate glass of ice. You pour it over yourself — that is the correct way.

situation.en: You've ordered coffee at nine in the morning and they expect you to eat.

question.en: Anything to eat with the coffee?

likelyReply.en: I'll have it out in a second.

situation.en: You're at the bar and want to settle up for your coffee.

categories.title: Starting a convo/basic survival
categories.description: Q → A → what they'll probably say

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You want to get a stranger's attention politely.

exchanges.notes: Used to get someone's attention.

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: Someone you've just met asks where you're from.

exchanges.notes: "Y tú?" is your natural follow-up here, not their reply.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You need help and want to check whether they speak English.

exchanges.notes: This exchange flips — the local answers this one.

situation.en: Someone asks how long you've been in the country.

question.en: How long have you been here?

likelyReply.en: What do you think of it?

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: Someone says something and you don't catch it.

exchanges.notes: "No te he entendido" blames the moment rather than your Spanish — softer than "no entiendo".

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You don't know a word and want to ask what it is.

question.en: How do you say __ in Spanish?

exchanges.notes: The local answers first here with "Se dice __", then checks your understanding.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You're leaving a casual conversation.

exchanges.notes: Closing line to end the conversation.

situation.en: Someone answered too fast and you got none of it.

question.en: Sorry, could you say that again?

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: Someone asks which football team you support.

answers.es: No entiendo mucho, pero me gusta el ambiente.
answers.en: I don't know much, but I love the vibe.

exchanges.notes: "El Madrid" and "el Barça" are the big two; fútbol is instant small talk.

situation.en: Someone asks whether you watched last night's game.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You need to leave, but you enjoyed meeting them.

question.es: Me tengo que ir, pero encantado/a.
question.en: I've got to go, but nice meeting you.

likelyReply.en: Likewise! Hope we run into each other again.

exchanges.notes: A warm, standard way to wrap up a chat.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: It's getting late and you want to wrap up warmly.

question.es: Se me hace tarde, otro día seguimos.
question.en: It's getting late, let's pick this up another day.

exchanges.notes: "Otro día" is a soft, polite way to bail.

situation.en: You've walked into a bar with the match on and someone turns to you.

answers.en: No idea, I've just got here.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: A decision has gone against the home side and the bar erupts.

question.en: What a robbery — that was never a foul.

exchanges.notes: The all-purpose Spanish complaint about a referee. Said out loud in a bar, it buys you agreement from strangers.

situation.en: They're talking football and you have nothing to contribute.

question.es: Yo del fútbol no entiendo, pero me apunto.
question.en: I know nothing about football, but I'm in.

situation.en: It's late and someone proposes one final drink.

question.en: Shall we have one last one?

answers.en: Go on then — the last one.
I'm going to call it there.

likelyReply.en: The last one is always a lie.

note.es: Slang changes by country. If something feels risky, ask: ¿Se dice así aquí?
note.en: Do people say it like that here?

phrases.en: No way / that's intense.
No way / not even as a joke.
I'm all in / I'm at full energy (Spain).
I don't care.
What a shame.
It's cool.
I mean / like — constant, and fills the same slot as en plan.
The thing is… — the universal excuse-opener, and arguably the most Spanish construction there is.
You're a legend (Spain).
You're amazing!
I'm obsessed / I love it (Spain).
Boom! / there you go! — celebration.
Good vibes / bad vibes. Foundational — "me da mal rollo" is a bad feeling about something.
Get out of here! — disbelief.
You wouldn't believe it — an intensifier for a story.
I'm cracking up.
A lot.
Like… (filler).
Loads. Madrid-leaning, understood everywhere.
Unbelievable — "es de flipar".
Packed, rammed — "el bar está petado".
Full on / all out.
No chance — a notch more casual than ni de broma.
Seriously / a fortune — "cuesta tela" is it costs a bomb.

subsections.title: The glue — what holds a Spanish sentence together

phrases.en: Let's see / right then — opens a sentence while you think.
Anyway / well, that's that. Closes a conversation.
Oh go on then — agreeing reluctantly, or nudging someone along.
No way / not at all. Much gentler than ni de broma.
Yeah yeah, okay okay — doubling it adds a note of impatience.
Anyway, so… — picking a story back up.
Come on / well now. A sentence-opener, whoever you're talking to.
I can't face it / it's awkward for me. Untranslatable and extremely common.
Loads / really — the defining Madrid intensifier. "Mazo bueno."
The house / my place.
The jacket — any jacket.
Dude / mate. Retro, and still very much heard.
Brilliant. Deliberately old-fashioned, and it always gets a laugh.
To be on the ball / paying attention.
To bail — "me piro" is I'm off.
A born-and-bred Madrileño, three generations deep.
Good morning. The single highest-return word in Barcelona.
Good afternoon / good evening.
Please.
Thank you / you're welcome.
Goodbye.
Let's go!
Come on! — the Catalan cousin of venga.
Wow, that's something! Untranslatable, and unmistakably Catalan.

subsections.title: Barcelona — what things are called here

phrases.en: A cortado — what the menu will actually say.
A ham-and-cheese toastie. On every menu, and visitors never order it.
To knock off work — "a quina hora plegues?"
A dreamer with their head in the clouds — literally an "omelette-dreamer".
To make a fool of yourself — literally "to do the peach".
City folk playing at countryside. Affectionately mocking.
How amazing!
Careful — not in front of them. Literally "there's laundry hanging out".
Roughly: "damn/f*ck" (Spain).
Sh*t.
Damn! / Bloody hell! (strong exclamation, Spain)
Darn it! — the version you can say in front of children.
Blimey! — literally "oysters", and the child-safe swap for hostia.
Sugar! — literally "Wednesday", started so you don't finish mierda.
Darn it! — softens the much ruder me cago en…
What a mess / unbelievable.
You're so annoying.
Go to hell (aggressive).
A bore — someone who sticks to you and won't come off.
A drag.
To be tedious.
To be fed up to here.
To have some nerve — "¡qué morro!"
A cheeky chancer.
Sorry, it slipped out.
I was joking, all right?
No hard feelings — literally "without bitterness".
I didn't mean you.

phrases.es: Se me ha ido la olla.
phrases.en: I lost the plot — literally "my pot has gone".
Sorry, I went too far.
I wasn't trying to intrude.
I take it back.

note.es: Tip: keep it short, smile, and don't overdo it. Consent and context matter.

phrases.en: You're handsome/beautiful.
That looks great on you.
I love your style.
You have a beautiful smile.
You seem like good people.

phrases.es: Contigo se habla muy a gusto.
phrases.en: You're really easy to talk to.
You've got a real spark to you.
I really like you — as a person, not as a line.
You're very attractive.
I like you.
Can I buy you a drink?
Shall we go somewhere else?
Are you staying a bit longer?
I'd love to see you again.
Shall we meet up another day?

phrases.es: Ha sido una noche muy buena.
phrases.en: That's been a really good night.
Can I tell you something?
If it makes you uncomfortable, I'll stop.
Is that okay with you?
Do you want me to go?
Tell me if it's too much.
Can I sit down?
Would you rather be on your own?
Are you comfortable?

subsections.title: Reading the room (into it or just polite?)

phrases.en: Green light: shall we grab a drink? (mutual interest).

phrases.es: Me lo estoy pasando genial contigo.
phrases.en: Green light: I'm having a great time with you.
Low-pressure modern move: can I get your Instagram?

phrases.es: Es que he venido con mis amigos.
phrases.en: Soft brush-off: the thing is, I came with my friends.

phrases.es: Eres majo/a, pero no me interesa.
phrases.en: Clear no: you're nice, but I'm not interested.

phrases.es: Sin problema, que lo pases bien.
phrases.en: The graceful exit: no problem, have a good one.
I'll message you — which means they won't.
I'm going back to my group.

categories.title: Getting around (taxi + metro)
categories.description: Q → A → what they'll probably say

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You've landed and you're looking for where the taxis are.

question.es: Perdona, ¿dónde está la parada de taxis?
question.en: Excuse me, where's the taxi rank?

answers.en: Out the doors, on the right.

exchanges.notes: Swap taxis for autobús or tren and the question still works.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: Before getting in, you want to know what a taxi into town costs.

question.en: How much is it to the centre?

exchanges.notes: Ask before the bags go in the boot, not after.

situation.en: You've landed and want the metro rather than a taxi.

question.es: ¿Dónde se coge el metro al centro?
question.en: Where do I get the metro into town?

situation.en: The officer at passport control puts a hand out.
You need to find the baggage belts.

question.en: Where do I collect my bags?

answers.en: Belt four, right at the end.

situation.en: You have no euros at all and want a cash machine.

question.en: Is there a cash machine around here?

answers.es: Justo al lado de la farmacia.

situation.en: You want a transport ticket and can't see where they're sold.

question.en: Where do I buy a ticket?

situation.en: Customs stops you on the way out.
You get into a taxi and the driver asks where you're going.

answers.es: A la calle __, número __, por favor.

situation.en: The driver suggests a route and checks it's fine with you.

answers.en: I'd rather go via __ if possible.

situation.en: The meter isn't running and you want it switched on.

question.en: Can you turn on the meter?

situation.en: You're paying the taxi driver and have no cash on you.

likelyReply.en: I'll charge you when we arrive.

situation.en: You've arrived and want the driver to stop here.
You need a receipt for the ride.
You're at the car with a heavy case and the boot is shut.
You're late and want the quickest route rather than the prettiest.

question.es: Mejor por el centro, que corre prisa.
question.en: Through the centre if you can — I'm in a hurry.

answers.es: A esta hora mejor por la ronda.
answers.en: At this hour the ring road is faster.

situation.en: You're on the street looking for the metro.

question.es: Perdona, ¿dónde está la entrada del metro?

situation.en: You know where you're going but not which line to take.

question.en: I want to go to __. Which line?

situation.en: You've been told to change lines and need to know where.
You want to know how far your stop is.
You're on the metro and think you've boarded the wrong way.

question.es: Creo que voy en dirección contraria.
question.en: I think I'm going the wrong way.

answers.es: Te bajas en la siguiente y cambias de andén.
answers.en: Get off at the next one and change platforms.

situation.en: An inspector asks to see your ticket mid-journey.
It's late and you need to know if you can still get back.

question.en: What time does the metro close?

situation.en: You're on a platform and want someone to confirm you're on the right side.

answers.es: No, es el andén de enfrente.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You're unsure you're heading the right way and stop someone.

question.en: Excuse me, is this the way to __?

likelyReply.es: Sí, todo recto y a la izquierda.
likelyReply.en: Yes, straight ahead and to the left.

exchanges.notes: "Todo recto" = straight ahead.

situation.en: You've been pointed in a direction and want to know how far.
You have no idea where you are and need help.

likelyReply.en: Where do you want to go?

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: It's late, there are three of you, and you need a taxi to the centre.

question.en: Can you take us to the center? There's three of us.

likelyReply.es: Subid, pero de tres como mucho.

exchanges.notes: Splitting the fare: "pagamos a medias" = let's split it.

situation.en: You want the driver to drop you right where you are.

question.en: Just drop us right here, thanks.

situation.en: Directions in Spanish are coming too fast for you.

question.en: Can you point it out on the map?

answers.en: We're here — you want to be there.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: The metro has shut and you're a long way from your bed.

question.en: Does a night bus come through here?

exchanges.notes: Night buses are búhos — owls. Every big Spanish city runs them once the metro shuts, and they all leave from one central square.

situation.en: The street you've been sent down is dark and empty.

categories.title: At a restaurant
categories.description: Q → A → what they'll probably say

situation.en: You walk into a restaurant with one other person.
The host asks whether you've booked.
The host asks how many are in your party.
You've been told to wait and want to know how long.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: The terrace looks better than the dining room.

question.en: Can we eat out on the terrace?

answers.en: Yes, if you can find a spot.

exchanges.notes: Terrace tables often cost more than the same food inside. It is legal, and it is on the menu in small print.

situation.en: They pick up menus and ask where you'd like to sit.

likelyReply.en: I'll put you at that one there.

situation.en: There's a queue and you want to know whether to bother.
You've been seated next to the kitchen door.

question.en: Could we move to another table?

answers.en: Of course — sit wherever you like.

situation.en: The waiter comes over to take your order.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You want the waiter to recommend something local.

question.es: ¿Qué es lo más típico de aquí?

answers.es: La tortilla / las croquetas / el pulpo…

likelyReply.es: Está muy bueno. / Es lo que más sale.
likelyReply.en: It's really good / it's what people order most.

exchanges.notes: The staff answers this one — you're asking for a recommendation.

situation.en: The waiter asks whether you want bread.
You want a dish made without one of its ingredients.
Something on the menu is a word you've never seen.
You need the kitchen to know about an allergy before you order.

question.es: Soy alérgico/a a los frutos secos.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: It's a weekday lunchtime and you want the good-value option.

question.en: Is there a set lunch menu?

answers.en: Yes, thirteen euros with a drink.

exchanges.notes: Menú del día is the weekday lunch deal: starter, main, bread, a drink and dessert or coffee. Always the best value on the menu.

situation.en: You've given your starter and they're waiting on the rest.
A dish arrives that you didn't order.

question.es: Perdona, creo que esto no es lo mío.

answers.es: Uy, perdona. Ahora te lo cambio.
answers.en: Oh, sorry. I'll change it now.

situation.en: Something's wrong with your dish and you want it swapped.
Your food has arrived cold.

likelyReply.es: Cuánto lo siento, te lo caliento.
likelyReply.en: So sorry, I'll heat it up for you.

situation.en: The waiter puts down a plate that isn't yours.

question.es: Yo esto no lo he pedido.

likelyReply.es: Uy, perdona, me he confundido de mesa.
likelyReply.en: Oops, sorry, I mixed up the table.

situation.en: The table beside you was served before you and you got there first.

question.en: We're still waiting for our food.

situation.en: The bread went in about ninety seconds.

question.es: ¿Nos traes un poco más de pan?
question.en: Could you bring a bit more bread?

situation.en: You need the toilet and there's no sign anywhere.

answers.en: At the back on the right.

situation.en: The table wants the same again.

question.en: Could you bring us another round?

situation.en: You've finished eating and want to pay.
You're paying with others and want to split the bill.

answers.en: Of course, I'll split it for you.

likelyReply.en: Tell me how much each person pays.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You don't know whether you're expected to leave anything extra.

answers.en: Yes, there's no need to tip.

exchanges.notes: Spain barely tips. Rounding up, or leaving the coins from your change, is plenty and nobody expects more.

situation.en: There's a line on the bill nobody at the table ordered.

question.es: Creo que hay un error en la cuenta.
question.en: I think there's a mistake on the bill.

situation.en: You've got no card on you but your phone is in your hand.

question.en: Can I pay with my phone?

situation.en: You want to get the whole table's bill.
You're paying cash and don't want the coins back.

answers.en: Thanks very much — see you next time.

situation.en: They take the card machine away and check in on the meal.

categories.title: Checking in (hotel/hostel/Airbnb)
categories.description: Arriving, room problems, and getting out on time.

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: You arrive at your hotel and reception asks if you've booked.

likelyReply.en: Great, can I have your passport?

exchanges.notes: They'll ask for a passport or DNI (ID) at check-in.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You've arrived before check-in and are carrying your bags.

question.es: ¿Puedo dejar las maletas hasta la hora de entrada?
question.en: Can I leave my bags until check-in time?

likelyReply.en: Sure, we'll keep them for you.

exchanges.notes: "La entrada" = check-in; "la salida" = checkout.

situation.en: You want to know when you have to be out of the room.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: The air conditioning in your room has stopped working.

likelyReply.en: Sorry, I'll send someone right away.

exchanges.notes: Swap in "la ducha" (shower), "la tele" (TV), "la calefacción" (heating).

situation.en: You want to know whether breakfast comes with the room.

likelyReply.es: Sí, de ocho a diez. / No, son cinco euros aparte.
likelyReply.en: Yes, from eight to ten. / No, it's five euros extra.

situation.en: You need to get online and want the wifi password.

question.en: Can I have the wifi password?

likelyReply.es: Está en la tarjeta de la habitación.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: Your flight is late in the day and you want to stay longer.

question.en: Can I do a late checkout?

likelyReply.es: Hasta las dos, sin coste. / Son diez euros más.
likelyReply.en: Until two, no charge. / It's ten euros more.

exchanges.notes: "Late checkout" is used as-is in Spain; "salida tardía" also works.

situation.en: You'd rather not carry your passport around all day.

question.en: Is there a safe in the room?

categories.title: Shopping, markets & haggling
categories.description: Shops, sizes, paying — and haggling at the market.

situation.en: You walk into a shop and an assistant offers to help.

question.en: Can I help you with anything?

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: Something catches your eye and you want to know the price.

exchanges.notes: "¿Cuánto vale?" is very common in Spain (also "¿Cuánto cuesta?").

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: The assistant asks what size you take.

answers.es: No estoy seguro/a, ¿me la puedo probar?
answers.en: Not sure, can I try it on?

likelyReply.en: The fitting rooms are at the back.

exchanges.notes: "Talla" = clothes size; "número" = shoe size.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You're at a shop till and want to check the shop takes cards.

likelyReply.es: Sí, a partir de cinco euros.

exchanges.notes: Some small shops have a card minimum.

situation.en: You like the cut but not the colour.

question.en: Do you have it in another colour?

situation.en: You're buying on impulse and want to know if you're stuck with it.
An assistant comes over while you're browsing.

question.en: Are you looking for anything in particular?

answers.en: Thanks, I'll have a look myself.

likelyReply.en: Just say if you need anything.

situation.en: You want it but you can't carry it around all afternoon.

question.en: Could you hold it for me until later?

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: A market stallholder calls you over and you want to know the price of the tomatoes.

question.en: Hey, handsome/beautiful! What can I get you?

exchanges.notes: "¿A cómo está(n)…?" is the market way to ask produce prices.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You want two of something and are angling for a discount.

question.es: ¿Me haces un precio si llevo dos?
question.en: Can you give me a deal if I take two?

likelyReply.es: Va, te los dejo en cinco.
likelyReply.en: Alright, I'll give them to you for five.

exchanges.notes: Haggle at flea markets (El Rastro), not in normal shops.

situation.en: The price is higher than you'd like.

question.es: Uf, es un poco caro. ¿Es tu último precio?
question.en: Oof, a bit pricey. Is that your best price?

likelyReply.es: Te lo dejo en __ y ya está.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You've decided to buy it and want it bagged.

question.es: Me lo llevo. ¿Me lo pones en una bolsa?
question.en: I'll take it. Can you bag it?

likelyReply.en: Here you go, and thanks, love.

exchanges.notes: "Majo/maja" = nice/friendly, very Spain.

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: You walk up to a busy market counter where nobody is standing in a line.

answers.es: Yo voy detrás de la señora.

likelyReply.es: Pues yo voy detrás de ti.

exchanges.notes: Spain does not form lines. You call out to find who you follow, and you answer when the next person asks. Getting this right is the single clearest sign you've been here before.

situation.en: You're at the counter and know how much you want.

answers.en: There you go — half a kilo exactly.

situation.en: You're buying fruit to eat this afternoon, not next week.
You're haggling at a street stall and want to name a number.

question.en: Can you do it for five?

answers.es: Cinco y medio y es tuyo.

categories.title: Sickness & feeling hungover
categories.description: The morning after: the pharmacy, feeling awful, and how drunk you (say you) got.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You wake up with a splitting headache and go to a pharmacy.

question.es: Buenas, ¿me das algo para el dolor de cabeza?
question.en: Hi, can you give me something for a headache?

exchanges.notes: In Spain you ask the pharmacist directly; many meds are behind the counter.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: Your stomach is in a bad way and you need something for it.

exchanges.notes: "Fatal" = terrible, extremely common in Spain.

situation.en: You think something you ate has disagreed with you.

question.es: Creo que me ha sentado mal algo.
question.en: I think something didn't agree with me.

likelyReply.es: Toma esto y bebe mucha agua.
likelyReply.en: Take this and drink plenty of water.

situation.en: You've caught the sun badly and need something for it.

question.es: Me he quemado con el sol. ¿Tienes algo?
question.en: I got sunburned. Do you have something?

likelyReply.es: Con esta crema, un par de veces al día.
likelyReply.en: This cream, a couple of times a day.

situation.en: A friend asks how your hangover is.

answers.en: I need a coffee and water.

situation.en: You want to know whether you need to see a doctor first.

answers.en: No, this one's over the counter.

situation.en: You're badly dehydrated and water alone isn't working.
You've got the box and don't want to overdo it.

question.en: How often do I take it?

phrases.en: A brutal hangover.
The comedown / feeling low after.
To party straight through to the next day, no sleep.
Outdoor group drinking in a park or plaza.

phrases.es: no vuelvo a beber (en la vida)
phrases.en: I'm never drinking again (ever) — everyone lies.
To feel wrecked and faintly ill — literally "a cut-up body".
The guilt hangover — last night replaying, on a loop.
To take the edge off — literally "to kill the little worm".

categories.title: Robbed & emergencies
categories.description: When things go wrong: theft, lost stuff and getting help fast.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: Your wallet has just been stolen and you need help.

likelyReply.es: ¿Dónde ha sido? Tienes que poner una denuncia.
likelyReply.en: Where did it happen? You need to file a report.

exchanges.notes: "Poner una denuncia" = file a police report; you need it for insurance.

situation.en: You've lost your phone or your passport.

question.es: He perdido el móvil / el pasaporte.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You need to find the nearest police station.

exchanges.notes: "Comisaría" = police station. Spain's emergency number is 112.

situation.en: You've been separated from the people you're with.

question.es: ¿Me ayudas, por favor? No encuentro a mi grupo.
question.en: Can you help me? I can't find my group.

likelyReply.en: Calm down, can you call them?

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: Someone needs medical help urgently.

question.es: Necesito un médico. / Llama a una ambulancia.
question.en: I need a doctor. / Call an ambulance.

exchanges.notes: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number, free from any phone.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: Your insurer won't pay out without a crime number.

question.en: I want to file a report.

answers.es: Pasa, que te tomo los datos.
answers.en: Come through, I'll take your details.

exchanges.notes: The denuncia is what your insurer will ask for. You can file it online or by phone as well as at the station.

situation.en: The officer taking your report asks what you saw.
Your passport is gone and you fly in two days.

question.en: I need to call my embassy.

situation.en: Your phone has died and you need to reach someone.

question.es: Se me ha quedado el móvil sin batería.

likelyReply.en: Do you want to use mine?

situation.en: You need to borrow a charger.

question.en: Do you have a charger I could borrow?

likelyReply.en: Yes, but it's an iPhone one.

situation.en: You want to borrow a stranger's phone for one quick call.
You have no data and need to work out where you are.

answers.es: Sí, la clave está en la pared.
answers.en: Yes — the password's on the wall.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: Roaming is costing a fortune and you want a local number.

question.en: Where can I buy a SIM card?

answers.es: En el estanco de la esquina.
answers.en: At the tobacconist on the corner.

exchanges.notes: Estancos sell SIMs, transport passes and stamps. They are the most useful shop in Spain and nobody tells visitors they exist.

situation.en: The bar is cash-only and your pockets are empty.
You're stood on a corner looking visibly lost and someone stops.

likelyReply.en: I'll walk you to the stop.

situation.en: You're inside somewhere crowded and can't see a way out.

question.en: Which way do I get out of here?

answers.en: Through that door, at the back.

categories.title: For the girls
categories.description: Recognize creeps and catcalling, shut it down, and ask for help fast in Spain.

subsections.title: Creeps & catcalling — what it sounds like & how to shut it down (Spain)

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: A man shouts at you from across the street and you want him to drop it.

question.es: ¡Guapa! ¿Adónde vas tan sola? Anda, dame una sonrisa.
question.en: Hey gorgeous! Where you off to all alone? Come on, give us a smile.

exchanges.notes: In Spain these street comments are called 'piropos' — you owe zero reply. Keep walking and step into the nearest shop or bar. Emergencies: 112. Spain's free gender-violence helpline is 016 — it never shows up on your phone bill.

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: He won't take no for an answer and starts following you.

question.es: Qué buena estás, morena. Venga, tómate algo conmigo, no seas así.
question.en: Damn, you're hot. Come on, have a drink with me, don't be like that. (he starts following you)

answers.en: Screw you, asshole! Get lost! (very aggressive — Spain)

exchanges.notes: If he won't back off or starts following, get loud to pull attention and move toward people or staff. In many Spanish clubs and festivals you can 'preguntar por Ángela' at the bar — a discreet code that tells staff you need help.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: A man is reaching to touch you and you want to stop him before he does.

exchanges.notes: Say it loud and clear. Louder still: '¡Que no me toques!'

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: A stranger already has his hands on your waist.

exchanges.notes: 'Quitar las manos de encima' is the natural Spain phrasing for someone grabbing you.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: Someone has gripped your wrist and won't let go.

exchanges.notes: For when someone is holding your arm or wrist.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: Someone won't stop what they're doing to you and you need them to hear that you mean it.

question.es: Para. Esto no me gusta. No sigas, por favor.
question.en: Stop. I don't like this. Don't keep going, please.

exchanges.notes: A clear, firm 'no' — no need to be polite about it if you don't feel safe.

situation.en: A man has followed you along the bar and won't take a hint.

question.en: I only want to talk to you.

answers.en: Well, I don't. Leave me alone.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You want the fastest exit line, whether or not it's true.

exchanges.notes: It shouldn't work better than no. It often does. Use whatever ends it fastest.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You don't feel safe leaving alone and want someone to walk you to a taxi.

question.es: ¿Me acompañas hasta el taxi, por favor? No me siento segura.
question.en: Can you walk me to the taxi, please? I don't feel safe.

likelyReply.es: Claro, te acompaño. No te preocupes.
likelyReply.en: Of course, I'll walk with you. Don't worry.

exchanges.notes: Ask staff, a couple, or a group of women — not a lone stranger. 'Acompañar' = to go with / walk with someone.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: A man is following you and you want someone to walk you home.

question.es: ¿Puedes acompañarme a casa? Ese tío me está siguiendo.
question.en: Can you walk me home? That guy is following me.

likelyReply.es: Vale, vamos. ¿Quieres que llame a alguien?
likelyReply.en: Okay, let's go. Want me to call someone?

exchanges.notes: 'Tío' = guy (Spain). If you're being followed, head somewhere busy and with staff rather than home directly.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: Your drink doesn't feel right and you think it's been spiked.

question.es: Perdona, creo que me han echado algo en la copa. ¿Me ayudas?
question.en: Excuse me, I think someone spiked my drink. Can you help me?

likelyReply.es: Vale, siéntate aquí. Llamo a seguridad y a un médico.
likelyReply.en: Okay, sit here. I'll call security and a doctor.

exchanges.notes: Tell the bar staff, not just your friends. Spiking is 'sumisión química' in Spain; needle-spiking ('pinchazo') has also been reported. Keep the drink as evidence and get to 112 / a medic.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You need someone to call the police for you.

question.es: ¿Puedes llamar a la policía, por favor?
question.en: Can you call the police, please?

exchanges.notes: 112 reaches police, ambulance and fire, free from any phone.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: A man is harassing you and you want staff to know.

question.es: Ese hombre de ahí nos está acosando.
question.en: That man over there is harassing us.

likelyReply.es: Venid conmigo, os llevo con seguridad.
likelyReply.en: Come with me, I'll take you to security.

exchanges.notes: 'Acosar' = to harass. Say it to staff or security ('los de seguridad').

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: A man is crowding you and you want to flag it to someone.

question.es: Perdona, ese tío de ahí me está agobiando y me incomoda.
question.en: Excuse me, that guy over there is crowding me and making me uncomfortable.

exchanges.notes: 'Agobiar' = to crowd/overwhelm; 'incomodar' = to make uncomfortable. Natural, non-dramatic way to flag a creep to staff.

situation.en: You don't want to be on your own for the next few minutes.
You're heading home alone and want someone to know you arrived.

question.es: Te escribo cuando llegue a casa.
question.en: I'll text you when I get home.

categories.title: Nightlife — into the club & making friends
categories.description: The door, the plan, and making friends before the afterparty.

situation.en: You reach the door of a club and the bouncer asks about your group.

question.en: How many of you are coming in?

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You want to know whether there's an entry fee.

likelyReply.en: Ten euros with a drink included.

exchanges.notes: "Con consumición" = the price includes one drink.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You want to know how late the place stays open.

exchanges.notes: Spanish clubs go very late — 6am is normal.

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: The bouncer asks whether you're on a list or have tickets.

exchanges.notes: Being on a promoter's "lista" often means free or cheaper entry before a certain time.

situation.en: The doorman holds out a hand without saying much.
You've got no cash and the bar looks busy.

question.es: ¿Se puede pagar con tarjeta en la barra?
question.en: Can you pay by card at the bar?

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: The doorman looks past you and shakes his head.

exchanges.notes: Spanish doors are gentler than Berlin's, but arguing still ends it. Walk on and try the next place.

situation.en: You're carrying a coat you don't want to dance with.
Someone at the bar asks where your group is from.

answers.en: We're from the US, and you?

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You've been chatting to someone and want to invite them for a drink.

exchanges.notes: "¿Os venís?" = are you (plural) coming along?

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You want to know what everyone's doing tonight.

likelyReply.en: We're going to an afterparty, you in?

exchanges.notes: "After" = afterparty; "¿te apuntas?" = are you in?

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You want to ask someone out for a night out.

likelyReply.en: For sure! Where should we meet?

exchanges.notes: "Salir de marcha" = go out partying (nightlife = "la marcha").

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You're exhausted and want to head home.

exchanges.notes: "Me piro" = I'm out of here (casual).

situation.en: This bar has died and you'd rather keep the night going.

question.en: Shall we move on to another bar?

situation.en: Someone at the bar notices you're standing by yourself.
It's three in the morning and you have a train at eight.

question.es: Me voy ya, que mañana madrugo.

phrases.en: To go out partying (nightlife = "la marcha").
To be at an afterparty.
How cool!
Dude / girl — Catalan term you'll hear in Barcelona.
You in? / Are you joining?
To meet up / make plans ("¿quedamos?").
A joint / dive bar. "Irse de garitos" is bar-hopping.
Pre-drinks at someone's flat before you go out.

categories.title: How drunk are you? (Spain)
categories.description: The whole ladder, and the moments where you have to pick a rung out loud.

note.en: Spain grades this finely and talks about it cheerfully. Naming your rung honestly is normal — it is how the group decides whether you're getting a taxi.

phrases.en: Tipsy, pleasantly buzzed.
Tipsy and cheerful (cute, old-school).
Feeling it, a bit gone.
Drunk (the standard word).
To be drunk — "voy pedo" works for anyone (never "peda").
Blind drunk.
Wasted.
"Cooked" = hammered.
To get smashed.
I'm super drunk (very Madrid).

situation.en: A few drinks in, a friend checks how you're getting on.
Someone is working out whether to get you another one.
You stand up and the room moves more than it should.

exchanges.speaker: them

situation.en: Someone arrives at the table with a tray of shots.

exchanges.notes: "Ir servido" is the graceful refusal: it admits you're drunk without making it anyone's problem.

situation.en: You've found your limit and want to stop at it.

question.en: This is as far as I go.

situation.en: A stranger has noticed the state your friend is in.

answers.es: Va muy mamada, me la llevo a casa.
answers.en: She's hammered — I'm taking her home.

likelyReply.en: Shall I get you a taxi?

situation.en: It's the next day and you're owning up to how it went.

question.en: I ended up in a state last night.

situation.en: You're leaving and someone wants to know you'll make it back.

question.en: Will you get home all right?

situation.en: The round is going in and you'd rather skip this one.
It's your round and you want something soft without a debate.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You drove here and want that understood before anyone pours.

exchanges.notes: Spain's limit is 0.5, and 0.3 in your first two years of licence. Saying you're driving ends it — nobody insists.

situation.en: Someone won't take your first no about one more.

exchanges.speaker: you

situation.en: You've drunk far more than you've eaten and can feel it.

exchanges.notes: The 3am Madrid answer. The bocata de calamares is the city's own hangover-prevention device.

situation.en: You've decided the night is over for you.
A friend is pacing you and pushes a glass across.
You're outside the bar and in no state to work out a night bus.

question.en: Could you order me a taxi?

answers.es: Ya te lo pido, espera dentro.
